-    Clin Use: allergy sx (runny nose, sneezing, itchy/watery eyes, throat itching) · common cold sx · insomnia (OTC sedative)

-    Caution: marked drowsiness (↑ w alcohol/sedatives/tranquilizers) · ask doctor first: breathing problems, glaucoma, trouble urinating (enlrg prostate) · ⍉ use to make a child sleepy · excitability (children)

: cortisol, as well as other steroid hormones, binds to intracellular receptors – the steroid-receptor complex enters the nucleus and acts as a transcription factor to turn on certain genes, causing synthesis of specific proteins which are responsible for its physiological actions
Increases BG, increases protein catabolism from muscle/bone, antagonist of insulin
Inhibits number/activity of cells involved in inflammatory response
Inhibits histamine release from mast cells
Mineralocorticoid effects: salt/water retention, potassium loss
•Replacement therapy: adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease) and congenital adrenal hyperplasia (defects in enzymes for steroid hormone synthesis)
•Dexamethasone suppression test (DST): diagnosis of Cushing’s syndrome
•Treatment of chronic inflammatory diseases:  RA, ulcerative colitis, asthma, SLE, eye and skin inflammation
•Treatment of allergic reactions: drug, serum, and transfusion reactions
•Immunosuppression: prevention of graft rejection after transplantation

: synthetic purine nucleoside analog with activity against HSV (types 1 and 2), varicella-zoster virus (VZV), and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV); stops replication of herpes viral DNA by competitive inhibition of viral DNA polymerase (selective toxicity), incorporation into and termination of the growing viral DNA chain, and inactivation of the viral DNA polymerase
